newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Wembley says to sell key property assets.
newsitem.headline: Wembley says to sell key property assets.

text.p: Malaysian property developer and industrial concern Wembley Industries Bhd said on Wednesday it was planning to sell parts of its key property project in the capital city.

Wembley's executive chairman Ting Pek Khiing said the company was negotiating with three separate parties to sell its office, hotel and apartment towers in the Plaza Rakyat complex in central Kuala Lumpur.

"The office tower, we will sell the whole block...The hotel, we also sell the whole block and then the apartment, we are selling the whole block," he told reporters after Wembley's annual general meeting.
Plaza Rakyat is Wembley's key property development which is scheduled to be completed in March 1999.
It would contain a four-star hotel, a 79-storey office tower, a block for apartments and a budget hotel, and one million square feet for retail shops, restaurants and entertainment areas.
The company plans a marketing launch for its retail space after foundations works are completed, he said.
Ting did not say why Wembley was selling the three towers.

The company in its 1996 annual report said contributions from the Plaza Rakyat project are not expected to be immediate due to a current surplus of office space and potential oversupply of retail space in the city.
Ting also said he would announce a restructuring of companies controlled by him very soon.
Stock market analysts have speculated that Ting will restructure his companies under his flagshup firm Ekran Bhd, the main developer of the $6.2 billion Bakun hydroelectric dam, to raise cash.
